chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated on the authority of his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abul-Qasim, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Rashid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Praise be to Allah who did not beget so as to be inherited, nor was He begotten so as to be associated [with in divinity].'
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'He begets not so He may be inherited, nor is He begotten so as to be associated' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the divine attribute of Tawhid by negating physical generation and procreation from Allah, a core tenet in Shia theology against anthropomorphism. It emphasizes that because Allah is not begotten, He has no need to associate partners with Him, distinguishing Him from created beings who inherit or are associated with lineage. The narration highlights the logical necessity of divine uniqueness, reinforcing that His essence is self-sufficient and free from the limitations of biological reproduction.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. Muhammad ibn `Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said on the authority of his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abul al-Qasin, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Barqi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Isa al-Yaqtini, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Rashid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn `Umar that
I heard Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) say “Praise be Allah who begets not so He may be inherited, nor is He begotten so He may be associated.”
